subject.title: fix(grep): bound file reads with size cap in default grep operations

question: Should default grep context intentionally omit context for matching regular files over 50 MiB at a fixed 50 MiB threshold, rather than implementing a bounded/streaming context strategy?
rationale: The patch safely prevents the unbounded read, but it establishes a new user-visible default for large matching files and the supplied evidence does not establish that this specific threshold and degradation mode are the chosen product contract.

options.title: Accept the 50 MiB bounded omission
options.body: Keep the guard, document the intended degraded context behavior in review evidence, and require a real default-grep demonstration before merge.

options.title: Use bounded context extraction
options.body: Replace whole-file reads with an implementation that extracts only needed context so large text files can still show surrounding lines without the fixed omission.

options.title: Pause for owner direction
options.body: Hold the PR until the agents-tool owner selects the intended large-file context contract and threshold.

recommendation.title: Accept the 50 MiB bounded omission
recommendation.body: Keep the guard, document the intended degraded context behavior in review evidence, and require a real default-grep demonstration before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The only concrete ownership signal in the supplied evidence is the author’s direct work on this implementation and its test design; current-main history ownership was not available in the review evidence.
